correctness.rationale: The exact characteristic polynomial and six-permutation second-moment average reconstruct from stated normal vectors and updates. Analytic derivative/discriminant arguments prove unique global minimizers on the complete interval (0,2); the Jordan formula is a real 2-by-2 nilpotent norm identity and the exact rational inequalities plus induction prove the all-k horizon reversal. The packaged SymPy verifier rechecks all nontrivial polynomial identities and root brackets, with finite two-epoch enumeration only as supplemental evidence. All quantifiers and deterministic-vs-expected metrics are defined.

originality.rationale: Inspected two directly relevant primary full texts plus a full open survey, searched exact formulas and conceptual aliases, and compared a published two-row Jordan-transient benchmark. Published general shuffled-SOR/RRK bounds, two-row optimized cyclic behavior, and the standard iid half-frame contraction do not directly imply the explicit three-line omega optimizers, exact reshuffle second moment, and reversal precisely between epoch 1 and all epochs >=2. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not certification of uniqueness.

value.rationale: This is the smallest redundant planar unit-norm tight-frame Kaczmarz system with three distinct lines, so fixed cyclic and reshuffling orderings are both natural meaningful choices. The sharp result resolves the practical conflict between first-epoch mean-square performance and asymptotic convergence: with each method tuned to its long-run optimum, fresh reshuffling wins at k=1 but loses for every k>=2. The exact formula simultaneously quantifies reshuffling benefit over independent draws and an approximately 40.7-fold optimal asymptotic squared-rate gap. This is a nontrivial structural benchmark rather than a generic textbook contraction bound; it may motivate horizon-aware row scheduling and overrelaxation selection. It does not claim a general algorithmic superiority theorem.
